title: Rabbi David Tawil: Life Lessons From Pirke Abot- "Conflict & Confrontation"

chapters.title: Introduction and Dedications
chapters.about: Dedications, community opening, and introductory remarks

chapters.title: The Relationship Business
chapters.about: Rabbi Tawil discusses his role as a rabbi and how life is fundamentally about relationships

chapters.title: Conflict and the High Holidays
chapters.about: Connecting the season of Teshuvah and forgiveness to dealing with relationship conflicts

chapters.title: Conflict Avoidance in Marriage
chapters.about: Using a dinner scenario to illustrate how couples avoid conflict and internalize issues

chapters.title: The Build-Up of Resentment
chapters.about: How bottled-up conflicts lead to resentment and eventual eruption

chapters.title: Finding Compromise
chapters.about: The importance of expressing true feelings to achieve genuine compromise and relationship growth

summary: Rabbi David Tawil discusses the importance of addressing conflict and confrontation in relationships rather than avoiding them. He uses a relatable example about a couple deciding on dinner to illustrate how avoiding conflict leads to built-up resentment, and emphasizes that confronting issues constructively is necessary for growth and forgiveness.
questions: Why do people tend to avoid conflict in relationships?
How does avoiding small disagreements affect a relationship over time?
What is the connection between confrontation and the period of Teshuvah and the High Holidays?
How can couples find compromise instead of bottling up their feelings?
